content:
alex: Hey team — Acme Corp POC asking for the full compliance onboarding checklist. specific asks: SOC2 Type II, an ISO excerpt if we have it, and a signed "pen test" attestation they can include in their vendor risk review. who owns the signed letter?
priya: I can own the pen-test letter template. we usually provide a 'pen-test authorization/attestation' signed by legal + security lead. redacted pentest report is usually fine. do they want the raw report or just an attestation?
alex: they asked for a signed letter + proof we do regular external scans. ideally both. customer legal also wants to know if we can give a window for them to run their own external scan against staging.
kim: staging IPs and creds are fine but must be ephemeral and scheduled. we need 48h lead time for firewall rules and to lock down KV access. also we need to be explicit about what endpoints are allowed.
ben: quick pricing note — if they want us to stand up a dedicated staging node for their external scan (isolation) that falls under reserved/dedicated pricing. confirm whether they expect shared staging or dedicated. could be ~1 week lead time for dedicated.
priya: for documentation I need: SOC2 Type II cover page (PDF ok), ISO27001 cert excerpt (if we have it), signed pen-test attestation on letterhead (we'll provide template), and a short note about vulnerability scanning cadence (static: weekly auth, dynamic: monthly external scan). redaction rules: remove IPs/creds and exploit PoCs.
alex: ok i'll ask Acme what they specifically need. can you drop the template + exact upload method here?
compliance-bot: pen-test template uploaded: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/templates/pen_test_attestation_template.docx :link: (access restricted)
priya: template is up ^. upload instructions: please use presigned S3 link or put into the secure evidence dshared folder (SAML-only). do NOT email reports. i'll create a minimal checklist: 1) SOC2 cover page 2) ISO excerpt 3) signed attestation 4) signed NDA (if they request full pentest report) 5) staging IP window + point contact.
kim: technical notes to include in the checklist for Acme: a) allowed scan targets (hostname list) b) allowed ports c) time window (UTC) d) contact for throttling/kill-switch e) whether auth scanning required. share example: ``hosts: staging.rw-acme.example.com``
alex: customer asked if we can sign their standard "third-party attestation" doc instead of our template. legal usually pushes back if it imposes extra liability. @priya — can legal sign theirs or should we ask them to sign our template?
priya: brief: we can review their doc but we rarely sign additional liability clauses. ask them to sign our attestation; if they insist, route to legal. i'll review their doc once received.
ben: logistics re upload — if they want to drop a redacted report for review, we need an SSO-enabled share link. raise a support ticket for temporary access if they can't use presigned URLs.
alex: timeline ask from Acme: they'd like everything by EOD next Tue to hit their procurement window. feasible?
kim: technically possible if we get confirmation today on whether shared staging or dedicated. 48h for firewall changes + 24h to validate. so in practice, earliest full readiness is 3 business days.
priya: I'll prep the attestation and checklist today. Alex, please forward legal contact and the customer's expected scope. i'll add a short note about redaction standards.
alex: putting names on this: priya -> attestation + checklist, kim -> schedule staging and presigned upload, ben -> pricing note & support ticket if needed. I'll update the customer and share their doc if they send one. :thumbsup:
priya: one more thing — we should include a short paragraph in the letter about our data handling for POCs (no data retention beyond X days in staging) — helps procurement.
alex: good call. i'll add that. thanks all.
ben: ping me if they push dedicated — i'll prep a quick estimate to avoid procurement delays.
compliance-bot: reminder: attach signed attestation (PDF) to ticket #POC-4521 when completed.
